--- license: apache-2.0 language: - zh - en - ja - ko - de - fr - es - it - ru - ar - fi - hi - id - ms - nl - "no" - pl - pt - sv - th - tr - vi - yue library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: text-to-speech base_model: Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b tags: - audio - text-to-speech - tts - voice-cloning - zero-shot - multilingual ---
[![GitHub](./assets/badges/github-badge.svg)](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS) [![License](./assets/badges/license-badge.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Demo](./assets/badges/demo-badge.svg)](https://edge0-ai.github.io/Audio8_TTS/realistic-0.6b/) [![arXiv](./assets/badges/arxiv-badge.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14776) [![Playground](./assets/badges/playground-badge.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air) [Languages](#supported-languages) · [Quick start](#installation) · [Serving](#high-throughput-serving-sglang-omni) · [Evaluation](#evaluation)
--- **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air** builds on [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b), delivering **substantially improved speech realism** while retaining its compact **0.6B** architecture and zero-shot voice cloning capabilities. This release supports **23 languages**, adding **12 languages compared with Preview**. It uses the same Transformers inference interface as Preview. This repository includes the complete model checkpoint, its 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and custom Transformers code. Try speech generation and voice cloning in the [interactive Playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air). Hosted on Hugging Face ZeroGPU; availability depends on the queue and your daily GPU allowance. ## Highlights - **Improved realism:** more natural prosody and expressive delivery, building on Preview. - **Broader multilingual coverage:** 23 languages, including 12 additions to Preview's 11 supported languages. - **Compact model:** 601 million main-model parameters, with the audio codec bundled separately. - **Flexible generation:** zero-shot voice cloning from a reference recording and transcript, or speech generation without a reference. - **GPU serving:** an SGLang Omni adapter with paged attention, dynamic batching, and an OpenAI-compatible speech API. ## Supported Languages | Coverage | Languages | |---|---| | Supported in Preview (11) | Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish | | Added in Realistic Air (12) | Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese | > **Note:** Language quality varies; see the per-language evaluation below. Benchmark coverage includes some additional languages and is distinct from the supported-language list. ## Model Details Audio8 TTS uses a DualAR architecture inspired by [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech). The slow AR transformer predicts one semantic token for each audio frame. The fast AR transformer predicts the frame's codec codebooks, conditioned on the slow hidden state and preceding codebooks. | Component | Configuration | |---|---| | Main model | 601,159,424 parameters, excluding the codec | | Slow AR | 24 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Fast AR | 4 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Acoustic tokens | 10 codebooks, 4,096 entries per codebook | | Codec | 44.1 kHz, 2,048 samples per model frame (~21.5 frames/s) | | Context | Up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions | The bundled codec handles both reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding, so no additional codec checkpoint is required. The **0.6B** size refers to the main DualAR model; the codec is excluded from that parameter count. --- ## Installation Python 3.10 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended. ```bash pip install "torch>=2.5.0" "torchaudio>=2.5.0" \ "transformers>=4.57.0,<5" "soundfile>=0.12" "safetensors>=0.4" ``` The Transformers release package was smoke-tested with PyTorch 2.8.0 and Transformers 4.57.3 on an NVIDIA H20 using BF16. Checks covered model loading, English and Chinese generation with and without reference audio, and generation in Arabic, Cantonese, Portuguese, and Russian. These are runtime checks, separate from the benchmark results below. ## Usage The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the files in this repository, then load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Zero-shot voice cloning Use a clean reference recording. Its transcript must match the spoken content exactly. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["Welcome to Audio8 TTS. It is wonderful to hear from you."], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["The exact transcript of the reference recording."], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` ### Generation without a reference Replace the processor call above with: ```python inputs = processor( text=["This utterance does not use a reference voice."], return_tensors="pt", ) ``` Then move the inputs to the model device and run the same generation and decoding steps. For command-line inference, batching, and supervised fine-tuning, see the [Audio8 TTS repository](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS), using `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air` as the model path. ## High-throughput serving: SGLang Omni The [SGLang Omni adapter](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) provides GPU serving for Audio8 TTS. It is installed as an independent model plugin and does not overwrite SGLang Omni core files. | Capability | Support | |---|---| | Attention and batching | SGLang paged attention and dynamic batching | | DualAR execution | Slow AR serving with a fixed KV cache for the Fast AR codebook decoder | | Voice cloning | Reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding | | API | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` service | Use the **0.6B** configuration, `sglang_omni/configs/audio8_tts_0_6b.yaml`, and set the model path to `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air` or its downloaded snapshot. The adapter supports generation without a reference and zero-shot voice cloning. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS#sglang-omni-serving) for compatible dependency versions, installation, server configuration, and API examples. > **Validation note:** Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air was tested on an NVIDIA H20 in BF16 for generation with and without a reference through the non-streaming speech API, with Torch compilation and CUDA graphs disabled. These checks validate runtime compatibility; throughput and streaming were not benchmarked. --- ## Evaluation Error rates are percentages (**lower is better**). Speaker similarity (SIM) is on a **0–1 scale** (**higher is better**). These metrics measure intelligibility and speaker similarity; they do not directly measure perceived speech realism. ### Benchmark summary **Audio8-TTS-Preview** and **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air**, both **0.6B**: | Benchmark | Coverage | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic Air error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic Air SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Seed-TTS | English / Chinese | 1.23 | 1.25 | 0.682 | 0.704 | | CV3 | 8 shared languages | 4.80 | 4.56 | — | 0.663 | | CV3 | 9 core languages | — | 4.86 | — | 0.661 | | MiniMax | 24 evaluated languages | — | 5.89 | — | 0.754 | > **Note:** Values are unweighted language macro averages. Preview results are calculated from its [published model card](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#evaluation), with SIM converted from percentages to a 0–1 scale. The two releases were evaluated separately. A dash means the corresponding result was not reported on Preview's card. > > Seed-TTS averages English WER and Chinese CER, excluding hard Chinese. The shared CV3 subset is Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, and Italian; the 9-language set also includes Russian. CV3 averages exclude hard subsets and the 13 additional languages. MiniMax averages all 24 evaluated languages, including languages outside the supported list. ### Reference comparison The following error rates come from the sources used in our technical report. Different evaluation pipelines and text normalization make this a reference comparison rather than a strictly matched ranking. A dash means that a result is unavailable in the comparison, not that the model lacks support. | Model | Parameters (B) | Seed-TTS EN/ZH error ↓ | CV3 (9) error ↓ | MiniMax (24) error ↓ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air** | **0.6** | **1.25** | **4.86** | **5.89** | | Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B | 0.6 | 1.12 | — | — | | Qwen3-TTS-1.7B | 1.7 | 1.01 | 7.73 | 27.41 | | Higgs Audio v3 | 4 | 1.11 | 4.41 | 2.74 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7 | 1.17 | 4.49 | — | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6 | 1.32 | 4.49 | 4.40 | | MOSS-TTS-v1.5 | 8.5 | 1.52 | 6.11 | 3.78 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5 | 1.67 | 6.89 | — | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3 | 1.41 | 5.35 | — | > **Sources:** Qwen Seed-TTS results are from the Qwen3-TTS report, linked from the [official Qwen3-TTS repository](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS); Qwen's CV3/MiniMax results, all Higgs Audio v3 results, and MOSS-TTS-v1.5's CV3/MiniMax results are from [Boson AI's evaluation](https://huggingface.co/bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b). Fish S2 Pro's MiniMax result is from the Fish Audio S2 report, linked from the [official Fish Speech repository](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech); its Seed-TTS/CV3 results and Higgs Audio v2's results are our reevaluations. MOSS-TTS-v1.5's Seed-TTS result and the CosyVoice3/VoxCPM2 results are compiled in the [VoxCPM repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM). Cross-project SIM values are omitted because speaker encoders and evaluation conventions differ. > **Parameter conventions:** Audio8's 0.6B excludes its separate codec; Qwen and CosyVoice use release labels; Higgs Audio v3 uses its nominal **4B** release label. The remaining sizes are rounded checkpoint counts used in our report (VoxCPM2 excludes its separate AudioVAE). These counts use different conventions across systems. ### Seed-TTS detail | Split | Metric | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic Air error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic Air SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | English | WER | 1.506 | 1.464 | 0.632 | 0.663 | | Chinese | CER | 0.950 | 1.029 | 0.731 | 0.745 | | Chinese, hard | CER | 11.510 | 12.797 | 0.687 | 0.702 | > **Note:** Preview values are from its [published Seed-TTS table](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#seed-tts), with SIM converted to a 0–1 scale. ### Multilingual detail

These hard subsets are excluded from the 9-language summary. Each of the 22 regular language rows contains 500 evaluation items. # Stable Audio 3 Small-Music — GGUF (for sa3.cpp)

GGUF conversions of [stabilityai/stable-audio-3-small-music](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-3-small-music)
for [**sa3.cpp**](https://github.com/betweentwomidnights/sa3.cpp) — a portable C++/GGML port of
Stable Audio 3, no PyTorch in the loop. Runs on CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, or Metal (Apple Silicon). The small-music model is a
lighter, faster music generator (SAME-S autoencoder, 0.5B DiT). Validated against the PyTorch
reference at cosine similarity ~1.0.

## Files

Multi-file model. Grab the **DiT** + **SAME** at your chosen precision and the **conditioner**, plus
the shared **encoder + tokenizer** from
[t5gemma-b-b-ul2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/thepatch/t5gemma-b-b-ul2-GGUF).

| component | file | notes |
|---|---|---|
| DiT (diffusion transformer) | `stable-audio-3-small-music-dit-0.5B-v1.0-{F32,F16,Q8_0,Q5_K_M,Q4_K_M}.gguf` | pick one encoding |
| autoencoder (SAME-S) | `stable-audio-3-small-music-same-s-v1.0-{F32,F16,Q8_0,Q5_K_M,Q4_K_M}.gguf` | **must match the DiT** |
| conditioner | `stable-audio-3-small-music-conditioner-v1.0-F32.gguf` | tiny sidecar (prompt padding + seconds_total) |
| encoder + tokenizer | → [t5gemma-b-b-ul2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/thepatch/t5gemma-b-b-ul2-GGUF) | **shared** across all SA3 variants |

> **note:** SAME-S needs an **even** `--frames` count (the packed sequence must divide the chunk size).

## Encodings

`sa3-generate --encoding` resolves the DiT and the SAME with the same suffix, so download the pair.

| encoding | DiT | SAME-S | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| F32 | 1751 MB | 413 MB | 2164 MB |
| F16 | 877 MB | 207 MB | 1084 MB |
| Q8_0 | 481 MB | 110 MB | 591 MB |
| Q5_K_M | 343 MB | 79 MB | 422 MB |
| Q4_K_M | 312 MB | 72 MB | 384 MB |

`q4_k_m` and `q5_k_m` promote the attention V, feed-forward down and embedding tensors to Q6_K;
`q8_0` is uniform. Every tier passes `sa3-quant-check` with `below-threshold=0` at cosine `0.990`
against the F16 reference, for the DiT and the SAME alike.

**Quantization buys footprint everywhere and speed only on some backends.** CUDA and Vulkan gain
roughly 33% end to end. **Metal is flat** — Q8_0 is 1.7% faster and Q4_K_M 2.1% *slower* than F16,
because the load-time saving and the added per-step dequant cancel out. On a Mac, pick a quant for
the memory, not for the speed.

## Usage

For use with [**sa3.cpp**](https://github.com/betweentwomidnights/sa3.cpp):

```bash
python tools/download_models.py --variant small-music --encoding f16

# --model resolves the gguf set in ./models by name
sa3-generate --model small-music --prompt "lo-fi hip hop beat, warm vinyl, mellow keys" --out song.wav
```

For a quantized set, pass the encoding to both — the downloader and the generator use the same names:

```bash
python tools/download_models.py --variant small-music --encoding q4_k_m
sa3-generate --model small-music --encoding q4_k_m --prompt "lo-fi hip hop beat" --out song.wav
```

## Performance

Roughly **1.7s for a 12s clip** at f16 on an 8GB laptop GPU (RTX 5070) — about 2× faster than the medium
model. The sliding-window decoder keeps long generations linear. Full numbers + levers:
[docs/BENCHMARKS.md](https://github.com/betweentwomidnights/sa3.cpp/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md).

## License

These are format conversions of [stabilityai/stable-audio-3-small-music](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-3-small-music),
whose weights Stability AI releases under the [Stability AI Community License](https://stability.ai/license):
free for organizations under $1M annual revenue, with commercial use, fine-tuning, and derivative works
permitted within that threshold (above it, contact Stability AI for an Enterprise License). Outputs are yours.
That license carries over to these converted weights.

The upstream [stable-audio-3 source code](https://github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-3) is released
separately under MIT. Pair these with the shared T5Gemma text encoder, which is Google's under the
[Gemma Terms of Use](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms).

## Relationship to the original

**Format conversions** (weights → GGUF) for inference in sa3.cpp — no retraining. See
[sa3.cpp/docs/DISTRIBUTION.md](https://github.com/betweentwomidnights/sa3.cpp/blob/main/docs/DISTRIBUTION.md).

# Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base

Turkish continual pretraining of [BreezeBlue/breeze-tts-2](https://huggingface.co/BreezeBlue/breeze-tts-2) for Turkish
prosody and pronunciation with Turkish/English code-switching. English/Chinese replay data was mixed in to preserve the
base model's English and Chinese (not re-benchmarked here). Zero-shot voice cloning, voice design and voice direction
work as in the base model.

## Architecture

Dual-AR text-to-speech, unchanged from Breeze TTS 2 (standalone checkpoint, no PEFT needed):

| Component | Details |
|---|---|
| Text encoder | T5Gemma 2 encoder (`T5Gemma2TextEncoder`, 26 layers, d=1152, 1.00 B parameters); the CPT's r=8 q/v/o LoRA is merged (78 modules); special-token rows `262144..262157` trained, Gemma vocabulary `0..262143` frozen |
| Projector | `text_encoder_proj`: linear 1152 → 2048 |
| Backbone (slow AR) | Qwen3 decoder (28 layers, d=2048, 1.41 B parameters) with its own 262,158 × 2048 text-token embedding (0.54 B); predicts RVQ codebook 0 + EOS every 80 ms |
| Depth decoder (fast AR) | 12 layers (d=1024, 0.43 B parameters), predicts codebooks 1–15 of each frame |
| Audio tokenizer | Qwen3-TTS 12 Hz tokenizer (`Qwen3TTSTokenizerV2Model`): 16 codebooks at 12.5 Hz, 24 kHz in/out, bundled in `audio_tokenizer/` |

Size: about 3.5 B parameters. The safetensors shards hold 3,483,206,497 bf16 values (backbone 1.41 B, text encoder
1.00 B, backbone text-token embedding 0.54 B, depth decoder 0.43 B, a Mimi `codec_model` 0.10 B, heads and projector
0.01 B). The shard index's `total_parameters` field reports 3,466,363,713, the same value as the upstream checkpoint.

Training recipe: Phase 1 acoustic warm-up (first 15% of steps, T5Gemma 2 LoRA not yet trained) → Phase 2 joint CPT
(T5Gemma 2 r=8 q/v/o LoRA at 1.5e-5, full backbone 4e-5, depth decoder 1e-4, projector 1e-4, cosine decay to 10%),
tiered RVQ loss `[6, 4, 2, 1]` with depth loss ×2.5, WiSE-FT (α = 0.85) against the base weights, then Phase 3 DPO
on synthetic failure-mode preference pairs (LoRA r=16/32, β = 0.1; see the release notes). v2.0 was trained on
4× NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (RunPod): CPT data-parallel on every GPU, DPO on one.

Code-switching example. English terms stay in English spelling; numbers and times must be written out (verbalized)
before synthesis:

> Saat 14:30'daki Sprint Planning toplantısına 10 dakika kaldı, GitHub üzerindeki pull request'i mergeledim.
>
> → `Saat on dört otuzdaki Sprint Planning toplantısına on dakika kaldı, GitHub üzerindeki pull request'i mergeledim.`

The evaluations below verbalized text with the author's `normalize_turkish_for_tts` (`breeze_infer/tr_normalizer.py`),
which is not part of the public [breezeblue-ai/breeze-tts](https://github.com/breezeblue-ai/breeze-tts) repository;
with the public code, pass already-verbalized text.

## Benchmarks

#### 1.1. `Freya-TR-Eval` (`freyavoice/freya-tr-eval`, 495 conversational Turkish sentences)

[`freyavoice/freya-tr-eval`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/freyavoice/freya-tr-eval) (revision `1c30761f`):
406 `everyday` sentences generated by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` and 89 `short-native` texts sampled from Common Voice 17
and CoVoST2. Table 2 of the FreyaTTS paper ([arXiv:2607.09530](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09530)) scores every system
with Whisper-large-v3 after 8 kHz band-matching, so both **8 kHz band-matched** and **full-band** Whisper-large-v3
(faster-whisper) scores are reported, plus `wav2vec2-xls-r-300m-cv7-turkish` CTC CER (greedy, no LM), `UTMOS22-strong`
and `WeSpeaker ResNet34` cosine to the conditioning reference (`SIM ref`). The card's primary metric, semantic WER with
an LLM judge, was not computed. Breeze rows: production `breeze_infer.api` (`--fast-backbone-decode

UTMOS22-strong runs on 16 kHz input, once on the full-band audio and once after 8 kHz band-matching. Blind SNR is the

## Quickstart

This repository bundles both the model weights (`model-*.safetensors`, `audio_tokenizer/`) and the full Python inference and training codebase (`infer.py`, `breeze_infer/` with the Turkish normalizer `tr_normalizer.py`, and `train_tr/`).

```bash
hf download ersanbil/Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base --local-dir Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base
cd Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# Voice clone (reference audio + its exact transcript)
python infer.py . --ref-audio reference_tr.wav --ref-text "Referans kaydın birebir metni." \
```

## Community guide: training a character voice LoRA

A character adapter (backbone r=16 + depth decoder r=32 + `codebooks_head` r=16 LoRA, the script defaults) trains on one
RTX 4090 with the bundled `train_tr/` suite included in this repository (`train_tr/train_yesilcam_character_lora.py`,
`train_tr/train_breeze_tr_fsdp.py`, `train_tr/train_breeze_tr_dpo.py`, `train_tr/verify_and_wiseft_stage_bc.py`).
T5Gemma 2, the projector and the audio embeddings stay frozen, so pronunciation and code-switching are kept. The Gaddar
Kerim adapter took 29.7 min for 300 steps on 40 clips; the script's default is 400 steps.

1. Collect a few minutes of clean single-speaker speech (Gaddar Kerim: 40 clips, 2.8 min in total, 1.7–12.3 s each;
   no music, one sentence per clip, exact verbalized transcripts).
2. Encode the clips with the bundled `audio_tokenizer/` into `[T, 16]` codes: either a shard directory with
   `manifest.jsonl` (`utt_key`, `speaker_id`, `shard_file`, ...) or a `.pt` file holding lists of
   `{id, text, instruction, audio_codes, speaker_id, wav_path}` records.
3. Train (writes `adapter_model.safetensors` + `adapter_config.json` to `checkpoints/character_loras/<name>`;
   `--save-merged` also writes a merged checkpoint):

```bash
python train_tr/train_yesilcam_character_lora.py --base-tr-model Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base \
  --data my_character.pt --speaker-id my_character --character-name my_character --max-steps 300
```

4. Load it into the runtime. `merge=True` folds the adapter into the base weights; `breeze_infer` needs that when the
   adapter has a `codebooks_head` LoRA (the default), because its CUDA-graph depth decoder reads `codebooks_head.weight`
   directly. `merge=False` attaches or hot-swaps it as separate LoRA layers.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from breeze_infer.runtime import load_runtime
from train_tr.train_yesilcam_character_lora import load_character_lora_adapter

tokenizer, model, audio_tokenizer = load_runtime(Path("Breeze-TTS-2-Turkish-Base"), device="cuda", attn_implementation="eager")
config = load_character_lora_adapter(model, "checkpoints/character_loras/my_character", merge=True)
print(config["reference_audio"], config["reference_text"])  # default reference clip for cloning
```

Then synthesize exactly as `infer.py` does (`FastBreezeStreamingRuntime(model, audio_tokenizer, ...)`).

# Crele Nimbus v1

**A real-time audio decision model.** Ask yes/no questions about live audio in plain English,
and get an answer every 40 ms, plus events when an answer starts and stops. It also knows who
is speaking: the user, or someone else.

Stream audio in at any chunk size; each answer arrives about a tenth of a second after the
moment it describes. Give it a few seconds of the user's voice, and two built-in signals follow
the user and everyone else, live (see [The user's voice](#the-users-voice)).

Built for voice agents: barge-in, end of turn, background sounds, another voice in the room.

**Website:** [crele.co/models/nimbus](https://crele.co/models/nimbus) · **Code:** [github.com/Crele-AI/nimbus](https://github.com/Crele-AI/nimbus)

## The user's voice

Most voice activity detectors answer one question: is anyone speaking? Nimbus answers two,
because a voice agent needs to know whose voice it is:

| Signal | Answers |
|---|---|
| `user` | Is the user speaking? The voice you enrolled |
| `other` | Is someone else speaking? Any other voice: another person in the room, or a voice from a TV or a loudspeaker |

Both are always on, answered every 40 ms beside your own questions, with events when they
start and stop.

**What it makes possible:**

- **Barge-in from the user only.** Stop talking when the user interrupts, not when someone in
  the background says something.
- **The user's end of turn**, even while other people are still talking.
- **Talking over each other.** Both signals can be yes at once, so you can see when someone
  speaks over the user, or the user over them.
- **Someone joins.** Notice another person or a TV voice, and adapt.

**Enrollment** takes a few seconds of the user speaking, recorded live or from a file (the
playground records five). A speaker-embedding model compares the voices in the stream with
that one.

```python
session.enroll(user_voice_16k)     # float32, mono, 16 kHz, a few seconds of speech

for update in session.push(pcm_16k):
    for event in update.events:
        if event.question == "user" and event.kind == "started":
            ...                    # the user started talking: stop the agent's speech
```

Without an enrollment, the model has no reference: `user` answers `cant_tell`, and `other`
cannot tell the user apart from anyone else. Enroll before relying on either signal.

Shown live on a microphone: the user alone, another voice near and far, turn taking, and
overlapping speech.

The enrolled voice becomes a voiceprint, which is personal data in many places: get the user's
consent, and store it as you would any personal data.

## What you can ask

Any yes/no question about what can be heard right now, in your own words:

- "Is music playing?"
- "Is someone typing on a keyboard?"
- "Is someone whistling?"
- "Is a siren wailing?"

Every answer is `yes`, `no` or `cant_tell`, with its probability. The two voice signals,
`user` and `other`, are always on beside them.

## Tuning

Each question has four settings. The defaults suit most questions; change them per question.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| `threshold` | 0.70 | An event starts when the probability rises above this |
| `start_secs` | 0.12 | ... and stays up this long |
| `stop_threshold` | 0.35 | The event stops when the probability falls below this |
| `stop_secs` | 0.30 | ... and stays down this long |

- A sound is missed: lower `threshold` for that question, for example to 0.5.
- A question fires too often: raise `threshold`.
- An event does not stop: the probability is resting above `stop_threshold`; raise it.
- Speech turns split at short pauses: raise `stop_secs`, for example to 1 s.

## Speed

- About 0.7 seconds of compute per second of audio (real-time factor 0.7) on an Apple M4 Pro
  laptop CPU, one stream, with 8 or with 32 questions.
- Asking more questions costs almost nothing: going from 8 to 32 questions adds about 1 ms per
  80 ms step. The audio is processed once per stream; every question reads from it.
- An answer arrives 80 to 120 ms of audio after the moment it describes, plus compute.

## How well it works

Measured on 500 real AudioSet clips with the default settings:

- **Says yes about 0.2 s after a sound starts**: a median of 0.24 s over the sounds it caught.
  For speech, 0.21 s, with 97% of 181 speech onsets caught.
- **Ask in your own words**: questions worded in ways it never trained on scored 0.892 against
  0.911 for its own wording (mean AUROC over 40 sounds, the same clips).
- **Quiet in a silent room**: the highest resting answer across twelve sound questions was 0.03.
- **Tells the user's voice from other voices**: shown live on a microphone with the user alone,
  another voice near and far, turn taking, and overlapping speech (see
  [The user's voice](#the-users-voice)).

## Limits

- English questions only.
- One user voice per session. Without a voice clip, the two voice signals have no reference.
- Audio is 16 kHz mono. Each answer is about the last few seconds of audio.
- Some sounds are recognised better than others; tune `threshold` for the ones that matter
  to you, and test on your own audio.

## How it is built

- A streaming audio encoder distilled from Dasheng-Base.
- A speaker-embedding model, CAM++ from 3D-Speaker, for the two voice signals.
- Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, unchanged, which reads each question once.

# Audio-R1 — Qwen2.5-Omni-7B (LoRA)

LoRA adapter for [Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-7B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-7B) trained with **Audio-R1**, an RL post-training framework that uses audio self-supervised tasks as a source of verifiable rewards.

- **Paper:** [Audio-R1: Audio Reasoning through Reinforcement Learning on Self-Supervised Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34609)
- **Project page:** https://ijihoon98.github.io/Audio-R1/

## Training Details

| Hyperparameter | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Method | GRPO, 1 epoch, LoRA |
| Reward | accuracy (1.0 if the chosen letter is correct) + format (0.2) |
| Format reward | `<think>` and `<answer>` tags present |
| Optimizer / LR schedule | AdamW, cosine |
| Learning rate / warmup ratio | 5e-6 / 0.03 |
| Rollouts per prompt | 8 |
| Sampling temperature / top-p | 0.8 / 0.9 |
| KL coefficient β | 0.04 |
| Clip ε | 0.2 |
| Per-device batch × grad. accumulation | 8 × 4 |
| GPUs | 4 |
| LoRA rank / α / dropout | 8 / 32 / 0.05 |
| LoRA targets | all linear layers; audio encoder frozen |
| Precision / seed | bf16 / 42 |

## Usage

```python
import torch
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import Qwen2_5OmniForConditionalGeneration, Qwen2_5OmniProcessor
from qwen_omni_utils import process_mm_info

base = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-7B"
processor = Qwen2_5OmniProcessor.from_pretrained(base)
model = Qwen2_5OmniForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(base, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto")
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, "NearAndDear98/Audio-R1-Qwen2.5-Omni-7B").eval()

SYSTEM = (
    "Your response MUST contain two parts in this exact order: "
    "1. Your reasoning enclosed within <think> </think> tags. "
    "2. The final answer — a single letter for the correct option — enclosed "
    "within <answer> </answer> tags."
)
conversation = [
    {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM}]},
    {"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "audio", "audio": "example.wav"},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Question ...\n(A) ...\n(B) ...\n(C) ...\n(D) ..."},
    ]},
]
text = processor.apply_chat_template(conversation, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False)
audios, images, videos = process_mm_info(conversation, use_audio_in_video=False)
inputs = processor(text=text, audio=audios, images=images, videos=videos,
                   return_tensors="pt", padding=True, use_audio_in_video=False).to(model.device).to(model.dtype)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, thinker_do_sample=False,
                     use_audio_in_video=False, return_audio=False)
print(processor.batch_decode(out, skip_special_tokens=True)[0])
```

# Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b — LiteRT

[Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b) (Apache-2.0) converted to LiteRT (`.tflite`) for on-device text-to-speech with zero-shot voice cloning in 11 languages, at the model's native 44.1 kHz.

Audio8 TTS is a DualAR speech LM in the Fish Audio S2 Pro lineage: a 24-layer "slow" transformer predicts one semantic token per 46 ms frame, a 4-layer "fast" transformer predicts the frame's ten codec codebooks one at a time, and a neural codec (RVQ, an 8-layer windowed transformer and a causal upsampling ConvNet) turns the frames into audio. This repository holds the four graphs plus a Python host loop that reproduces the vendor's generation loop and sampler.

## Quick start (Python, desktop)

```bash
pip install ai-edge-litert tokenizers soundfile scipy numpy huggingface_hub
hf download litert-community/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b --local-dir audio8
cd audio8
python audio8_tts_litert.py --model-dir . --text "Hello from LiteRT, fully on device." \
    --voice voices/en_librispeech_1272 --out hello.wav
# Japanese with the bundled Japanese voice
python audio8_tts_litert.py --model-dir . --text "今日は天気が良いので、公園まで散歩に行きましょう。" \
    --voice voices/ja_funasr_example --out konnichiwa.wav
# clone your own voice from a 0.5-10 s clip and its exact transcript
python audio8_tts_litert.py --model-dir . --register-voice me.wav --ref-text "exact transcript of me.wav" --voice-out voices/me
python audio8_tts_litert.py --model-dir . --text "..." --voice voices/me --out out.wav
# generation without a reference voice
python audio8_tts_litert.py --model-dir . --text "This utterance does not use a reference voice." --out noref.wav
```

`--slow slow_ar_int4.tflite` selects the smaller slow AR. `--threads` sets the CPU thread count (default 4).

## Android

Sample app (Android): [`android/`](https://huggingface.co/litert-community/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b/tree/main/android) — type a sentence, pick one of the two sample voices or record your own for 10 s, tap Speak. The two autoregressive graphs run on the CPU (4 threads); the codec decoder runs on the GPU when its output passes a check against the same file on the CPU, and otherwise that file runs on the CPU. Galaxy S26, LiteRT 2.2.0, 2026-11-02, the codec decoder on the GPU: an 18-token English sentence became 5.99 s of speech at a real-time factor (RTF: generation time divided by the length of the speech) of 0.857 (median of 6 runs in two app processes, 0.828 to 1.229) and a 14-token Japanese sentence 3.44 s at 0.900 (0.880 to 0.904). Loading took 10.9 to 12.4 s, of which the decoder check took 7.8 to 8.2 s; in that check one 128-frame call of the decoder on the CPU took 2.84 to 2.85 s (four app processes), against 0.91 to 0.96 s for a sentence's 128-frame call on the GPU. When the check fails, the decoder runs on the CPU: on a Pixel 11 Pro with the first-published decoders put back on purpose, at thermal status 1 with its CPU frequency capped, right after other runs, one launch with a remembered failure loaded in 18.7 s, 13.5 s of it the CPU decoder's first call at load (a warm-up on all-zero codes).

## Files

| File | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `slow_ar_int8.tflite` | 552 MB | Slow AR (24 layers). Signatures `prefill_256` and `decode`; KV cache 2048 (the model's max_seq_len) as graph I/O; outputs the 4097 logits the sampler can pick (4096 semantic tokens + end-of-speech) and the normalized hidden state that conditions the fast AR. Dynamic int8 (per-channel) projections, int8 embedding tables. |
| `slow_ar_int4.tflite` | 386 MB | Same graph, blockwise-32 OCTAV int4 projections. |
| `fast_ar_int8.tflite` | 68 MB | Fast AR step (4 layers, 10-slot KV cache as I/O). Called 10 times per frame: position 0 takes the slow hidden state, positions 1-9 take the previous codebook token. Dynamic int8. |
| `codec_decoder_fp16_T128.tflite` | 262 MB | Codec decoder for up to 128 frames (5.9 s) per call; fp16 weights. Runs on the mobile GPU since 2026-11-02, when it was replaced by a rewritten decoder (see [Codec decoder on the GPU](#codec-decoder-on-the-gpu)). |

| `codec_decoder_int8_T128.tflite` | 132 MB | Codec decoder, all convolutions and projections int8 (export-time PT2E, fp32 codebooks); the CPU option. |

The sampler and the prompt format are the vendor's, so the loop accepts the same generation parameters (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9, top-k 50, max 512 frames by default).

## Codec decoder on the GPU

On 2026-11-02 the two fp16 codec decoders were replaced, under the same names, by rewritten decoders; the bytes first published are in [commit 56fcb491](https://huggingface.co/litert-community/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b/tree/56fcb491ebf03eb3a1a66615fedf6744015dd4c7), and `android/` changed with them. As first published, the two decoders give a wrong output on the LiteRT GPU accelerator: on a Pixel 11 Pro and a Galaxy S26 (OpenCL, LiteRT 2.2.0 and 2.3.2) and on an Apple M4 Max (Metal), at the GPU's default precision (float16) and at float32. If you downloaded the repository before 2026-11-02, download the two decoders and `android/` again: the app remembers a failed check together with the decoder file's size, so at its next launch it checks the new files and runs them on the GPU when they pass (seen on a Pixel 11 Pro where the first-published files had failed). The rewritten decoders carry three graph changes:

- Before two MUL operators whose non-constant operand (computed at run time) has rank 2 and the output rank 3, a RESHAPE gives the operand the output's shape. The GPU accelerator lays such a rank-2 tensor out differently from a rank-3 one, and the MUL then multiplied the wrong elements, at float32 too. The RESHAPE keeps the values and their order.
- Each RMSNorm squares its input scaled by 1/16, with epsilon scaled by 1/256 and the result scaled back. Unscaled, one square reaches 121,972.6 and the 1,024-channel sums of squares about 76,500, both more than float16 holds (65,504), and the output stops depending on the codes. Powers of two only move the exponent, so the CPU result is the same.
- The attention mask's −1e9 becomes −30000. In float16 −1e9 is −inf: with the other two changes in place, the 192-frame decoder's attention then gave NaN after the softmax on the GPU of an Apple M4 Max (Metal), and the output was constant.

On the Mac CPU the rewritten decoders give the original's output byte for byte on all 32 test code sequences (15 for 128 frames, 17 for 192). On the GPU at the default precision, their output correlates with that CPU output at 0.9996 or more on every speech test sequence of a Pixel 11 Pro and of an Apple M4 Max (Metal), and on the English and the Japanese one of a Galaxy S26. Decoded on the Pixel 11 Pro's GPU, every test sequence transcribes (whisper large-v3-turbo) with the same number of errors as the Mac CPU's output, and UTMOS22 is 3.956 against 3.960 (128 frames, 14 sequences) and 3.905 against 3.913 (192 frames, 16 sequences). The rewrite is [`codec_gpu_rewrite.py`](https://github.com/john-rocky/hf-to-litertlm/blob/main/audio8_tts_work/codec_gpu_rewrite.py) in hf-to-litertlm.

## Accuracy

Measured against the vendor's PyTorch implementation (transformers 4.57, CPU fp32) on 14 seeded sentences (6 English and 6 Japanese with a cloned reference voice, one of each without a reference), with the same random draws:

- The fp32 graphs reproduce the reference code sequence frame for frame on all 14 sentences; the codec decoder is bit-exact at torch level and within 2e-6 as `.tflite`.
- Speech recognition of the output (whisper large-v3-turbo) against the input text, and speaker similarity (TitaNet-L cosine) against the reference clip:

| configuration | en WER | ja CER | speaker cosine en / ja |
|---|---|---|---|
| PyTorch reference | 1.1% | 0.0% | 0.66 / 0.74 |
| `slow_ar_int8` + `fast_ar_int8` + `codec_decoder_fp16` | 1.1% | 0.0% | 0.68 / 0.76 |
| `slow_ar_int4` + `fast_ar_int8` + `codec_decoder_fp16` | 1.1% | 0.0% | 0.63 / 0.77 |
| `codec_decoder_int8` (reference codes decoded) | 1.1% | 0.0% | 0.67 / 0.73 |

The `codec_decoder_fp16` rows were measured with the decoders as first published; on the Mac CPU the rewritten decoders give the same output byte for byte on 32 test code sequences (15 for 128 frames, 17 for 192). The one English error is shared with the reference (the model drops the first word of one sentence). Quantized graphs sample a different but valid trajectory; per-frame agreement with the reference is not a meaningful metric for a sampled model, so the gate is the transcript and the voice.

## Performance

Measured, not estimated. The host loop is Python; the Android sample under `android/` runs the same graphs from Kotlin through the LiteRT CompiledModel API (its numbers are in the Android section above).

### Apple silicon Mac (CPU, 4 threads, ai-edge-litert 2.2.0, `audio8_tts_litert.py`)

Measured with the codec decoders as first published. The rewritten decoders give the same output byte for byte on the CPU of an Apple M4 Max (32 test code sequences); their times were not measured again.

| configuration | slow AR / frame | fast AR / frame (10 calls) | codec (T128 call) | RTF (median of 14) |

| int8 / int8 / fp16 | 9.0 ms | 9.2 ms | 1.43 s | 0.81 (0.73-0.98) |
| int4 / int8 / fp16 | 12.2 ms | 9.2 ms | 1.43 s | 0.92 (0.81-1.07) |
| int8 / int8 / int8 codec | 8.9 ms | 9.4 ms | 0.96 s | 0.70 (0.64-0.82) |

| graph | signature | backend | inference (avg) | init / overall memory |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `slow_ar_int8.tflite` | `decode` | CPU | 12.3 ms | 1077 / 1176 MB |
| `slow_ar_int8.tflite` | `prefill_256` | CPU | 241 ms | 1077 / 1249 MB |
| `slow_ar_int4.tflite` | `decode` | CPU | 10.0 ms | 610 / 709 MB |
| `slow_ar_int4.tflite` | `prefill_256` | CPU | 417 ms | 610 / 783 MB |
| `fast_ar_int8.tflite` | `step` | CPU | 0.97 ms | 127 / 127 MB |
| `codec_encoder_fp16_10s.tflite` | `encode` | CPU | 2365 ms per 10 s | 1206 / 1899 MB |

A 256-frame decoder does not prepare on the S26 GPU (`Dilated im2col buffer size overflowed`) and is not shipped; int8 convolutions do not run on that GPU; the AR graphs stay on the CPU (their codebook gather is not delegated). Memory figures are the benchmark tool's footprint; the multi-signature slow graph packs its weights once per signature.

The same phone on 2026-11-02, LiteRT 2.2.0 CompiledModel API. | graph | backend | time per call |

| `codec_decoder_fp16_T128.tflite` | GPU (OpenCL, 972 of 1,105 ops) | 937.6 ms per 5.9 s (8, 915.2 to 953.9) |

- On the GPU, the output correlates with the Mac CPU output at 0.9998 or more on the English and the Japanese test codes, and at 0.015 or less with the GPU's own output for all-zero codes. The CPU row gives the Mac CPU output exactly.
- During the CPU row the large cores were capped at 4.07 GHz at the lowest (4.74 GHz uncapped).

## Limitations

- The codec decoder is causal but its transformer stacks eight 128-frame windows, so decoding in windows is not sample-exact against a single offline decode; the host loop makes one T128 call for utterances up to 5.9 s, one T192 call up to 8.9 s, and beyond that T192 windows with 128 frames of left context (the same context the vendor's ONNX runtime uses).
- Voice registration accepts up to 10 s of reference audio (one static bucket); the reference transcript must match the audio.
- Prompt length + generated frames must stay under 2048 positions; the default cap is 512 frames (about 24 s) per call.
- Preview checkpoint: the vendor documents limited dialect coverage and sensitivity to noisy or mis-transcribed references. Generated speech can be misused for impersonation; obtain consent before cloning a voice and disclose synthetic audio.

# Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b-bf16 (MLX)

MLX conversion of [Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air)
(revision `925bbd4`) for Apple Silicon. Upstream published this model as Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b and
renamed it Realistic-Air on 2026-11-02; the weights are unchanged, so this conversion is the same model
under its new name. It is a 0.6B-parameter multilingual text-to-speech
model with zero-shot voice cloning and a bundled 44.1 kHz neural codec.

Realistic is an RL-tuned successor to
[Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b-bf16).
The architecture, codec, tokenizer and tensor layout are the same; only the language-model
weights differ. Anything that loads the Preview bundle loads this one.

- **Language model**: bf16 (as published upstream)
- **Codec**: fp32, converted from `codec.pth` to safetensors with weight-norm folded and conv
  weights in MLX (channels-last) layout. Byte-identical to the Preview bundle's `codec.safetensors`.
- **Architecture**: `arktts`, a DualAR transformer. A 24-layer slow AR predicts one semantic
  token per frame, and a 4-layer fast AR predicts 10 codec codebooks per frame.

Conversion parity vs the PyTorch reference (fp32, CPU, transformers 4.57.3):
- unit and block outputs within 1e-3
- reference-audio codec encoding is 100% code-exact
- greedy generation is token-exact over all 129 frames of the validation utterance
- decoded waveform max-abs 7.1e-6

## Usage (mlx-audio)

Requires [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) **≥ 0.4.7**, the first release with the
`arktts` model family.

```bash
pip install -U "mlx-audio>=0.4.7"
```

```python
import soundfile as sf
from mlx_audio.tts.utils import load

model = load("mlx-community/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b-bf16")

# zero-shot voice cloning: the reference transcript must match the reference audio
for result in model.generate(
    text="Welcome to Audio8 TTS, running on Apple Silicon.",
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    ref_text="Transcript of the reference clip.",
    temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=50,
):
    sf.write("output.wav", result.audio, result.sample_rate)
```

Without `ref_audio`, the model synthesizes with a default voice.

For Swift, the [mlx-audio8-tts-swift](https://github.com/xocialize/mlx-audio8-tts-swift) package
loads this bundle as `Audio8RealisticPackage`.

## Against the Preview checkpoint

These numbers come from our own A/B of this conversion against the Preview conversion. Both
cloned two English reference voices, with paired seeds, 2 draws per line, scored by
Whisper-large-v3-turbo and CAM++.

| | Preview-0.6b | Realistic-0.6b |
|---|---|---|
| error rate, en / zh / de / es / fr / ja (macro) | 0.0122 | 0.0126 |
| speaker similarity (CAM++) | 0.7212 | 0.7211 |
| pause time per line | 0.62 s | 1.52 s |

On those six languages the two models score the same on accuracy and voice similarity. Realistic
pauses more: its takes run about 13% longer, and all of the extra time is silence.

## Supported languages

- **Upstream's original 11:** Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian,
  Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish.
- **New in Realistic, measured at 1–7% error:** Finnish, Indonesian, Malay, Portuguese, Russian,
  Turkish.
- **Experimental:** Hindi, Norwegian and Swedish work but are uneven, at 10–25% error.
- **Not usable:** Arabic, Thai and Vietnamese. Thai falls into repetition loops.

These figures come from three lines per language, two voices and two seeds. Most of the
new-language lines were not checked by native speakers.

weights are the Preview's and carry the same license.
